name: Structure: Fix the rule that the hypothesis has no page and the correction is the check-in's
text_content:
P5, P10, P13, P15, and P48, the one thing on the S12 page a later session cannot revise at ordinary cost. A lead's reading of a person is said at the check-in, once, as an observation of behavior and impact, and is written nowhere; the only record of coaching is the person's own line; during service the only speech about a person's work is the range's call on the object; and no coaching record exists for any later mechanism to cite. A later session may design what Session 14 does with the count of a hypothesis heard and declined, what Session 15 does with a lead's own hypothesis and a lead who over-places, what Session 13 does with a review that opens on the person's lines, and what the reset does with the placed count; no later session may give the hypothesis a page, let a lead's observation onto any record about a person, move the correction into a room or onto the floor, or cite a coaching record this page ensures does not exist. Written as a structural rule on the mechanism map beside Session 6's four dimensions, Session 9's order of every read, Session 10's rule that the environment names no person in a room (86akht2k9), and Session 11's rule that nothing reaches the house that is not on a record first (17tn048qc3y). High.

Filed by Session 12 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmjba. Reasoning lives on the S12 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

comment.text: Session 14 keeps the rule whole inside the one mechanism it adds. The horizon window's first trigger reads the hypothesis count from the check-in dates and the record versions, because the hypothesis itself is written nowhere; the window block holds states, citations, the person's words, and the assessor's rows and has no field for a lead's hypothesis, observation, summary, or prediction; and the check-ins inside a window keep the check-in's spine and refusals whole. The window is the correction of a seat, not of a person, and the team reads it as canon's care-and-correction distinction applied to a seat, held for canon's owner (S14 finding 19.12). S14 page, sections 5.2, 5.6, 9, and 15; P16, P20, P33.
